item.title: DFC CEO Ben Black Discusses How DFC Is Investing in America’s Future
item.description:
DFC CEO Ben Black Discusses How DFC Is Investing in America’s Future anna.devanny Tue, 10/13/2026 - 17:26
Media Release
October 13, 2026

WASHINGTON – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black today spoke at a Heritage Foundation event titled “Investing in America's Future: Economic Statecraft in an Age of Global Competition.” The conversation was moderated by Heritage President Dr. Kevin Roberts.

 

On DFC’s mandate under the Trump administration: 

“In this era of increasing global competition, President Trump has tasked DFC with a critical mandate: DFC investments must deliver for the American people and serve as a powerful tool for strengthening the economic security of both the United States and our allies and partners.” 

“DFC will directly challenge our adversaries in the most strategically contested sectors by financing transactions that diplomacy and private markets alone cannot deliver... DFC will prioritize large, capital-intensive projects that are vital to U.S. strategic interests and highly transformative for our partners... And DFC will mobilize private capital through sophisticated financial structures that reduce risk for investors and create enduring American influence in critical sectors and regions.”

On the importance of bringing private capital alongside DFC investments: 

“Across all priority sectors, DFC’s financial products are uniquely suited to reducing investment risk and crowding in pools of private capital that dwarf our own balance sheet. It’s what distinguishes DFC’s approach from our adversaries and the ineffective models of the past. Chinese investments often lack independent private sector participation and the price signals and risk discipline that make projects truly commercially viable.” 

“State capital acting alone can never build dynamic markets the way that private capital can. Our global partners want to work with us because our model is better... The American free-market system is the engine that drives strength, growth, and goodwill around the world. It’s our greatest export and our greatest advantage.”

On advancing U.S. Super Intelligence dominance: 

“America has the best technology in the world and is winning the race for Super Intelligence, but the American SI stack cannot be exported to networks compromised by our adversaries. Last month, we approved an investment with Vodafone in Eastern Europe to modernize their networks and accelerate the replacement of Chinese telecommunications equipment, ensuring that when American companies operate abroad, their intellectual property and the information they transmit remains safe and secure.” 

“These telecom deals are challenging for our partners, who face immense pressure and threats of economic retaliation when attempting to diversify ownership of their networks. That is why we are committed to helping others adopt this model, especially in the Western Hemisphere, where China’s Digital Silk Road cannot be allowed to entrench its influence.”

On building energy infrastructure that advances U.S. strategic objectives: 

“Under President Trump’s leadership, the U.S. is the world’s largest producer of both oil and natural gas. Across the world, we see significant opportunities to build energy infrastructure that advances U.S. strategic objectives and provides reliable, affordable energy for our allies and partners.” 

“In June, DFC’s Board approved $1.5 billion for energy infrastructure across South and Southeast Asia, ensuring U.S. LNG and American equipment help power the growing energy needs of a region long dominated by our adversaries.”

These remarks have been lightly edited for clarity. You can watch the full event on Heritage’s YouTube page here.

###  

The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.

item.title: URIF Approves Additional Investments and Partnerships in Energy and Critical Minerals
item.description:
URIF Approves Additional Investments and Partnerships in Energy and Critical Minerals christopher.bull Fri, 10/02/2026 - 12:41
Media Release
October 2, 2026

 

WASHINGTON, D.C. and KYIV – The U.S.–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF) today approved a number of new investments to advance the shared economic and strategic interests of the United States and Ukraine. These investments will help secure critical supply chains, strengthen Ukraine’s energy resilience, and develop its critical mineral sector.

“URIF’s first investment in March demonstrated that it was open for business. Today’s board approval of additional investments in Ukraine’s critical minerals and energy sectors signals investor support for Ukraine’s recovery and future prosperity,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent.“These investments represent the continued realization of the vision behind the novel agreement that Prime Minister Svyrydenko and I signed in April 2025 to establish URIF and give America a direct stake in Ukraine’s long-term peace and prosperity”

“Today's Board meeting marks an important step forward for the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. These investments strengthen Ukraine's energy resilience, develop critical mineral resources, and support innovative Ukrainian companies. Together these projects are building the foundation for Ukraine's economic recovery and deepening the partnership between our countries,” said DFC CEO Ben Black.

“This round of investments shows the growing scope of the U.S.-Ukraine partnership, from energy and critical minerals to telecommunications and emerging technologies. For URIF, it is an important step in building a track record of investments that gives investors' confidence in Ukraine. We want to see more Ukrainian companies develop through this partnership and create new opportunities for the Ukrainian economy,” said Oleksii Sobolev, Deputy Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine.

The joint U.S.-Ukrainian URIF board of directors approved the following today:

  • Expanding Investment in Ukraine’s Critical Minerals: URIF will establish a joint investment platform with Ukrainian company BGV Group Management. The platform will seek to build a diverse portfolio of early-stage mining projects across Ukraine, supporting the development of Ukraine’s critical minerals sector. Its initial focus will be on identified assets of rare earths, beryllium, and zirconium deposits. This platform aims to significantly scale up Ukraine’s critical mineral production, creating Ukrainian jobs and investment opportunities for U.S. and Ukrainian companies and international investors, while shoring up secure supply chains of these vital critical minerals for U.S. and allied markets.
  • Restoring Heat and Power to Ukrainian Communities: URIF’s equity investment in a multi-site distributed combined heat and power (CHP) cogeneration platform will support the construction and operation of a series of community-scale energy hubs designed to restore electricity and heat supply damaged by the war. Once completed, the project is intended to provide heat and power to thousands of households, ensuring access to vital energy and heat in Ukraine as the conflict continues.
  • Enhancing Ukraine’s Energy Security: URIF’s debt investment provides financing for DTEK’s 200 MW/400 MWh battery energy storage system across six sites in Ukraine. The system is operational, with enough capacity to supply electricity equivalent to approximately 600,000 Ukrainian homes for two hours and provide the country’s power grid with greater resilience and stability. The project is built by DTEK, Ukraine’s largest private energy company, and leverages American energy technology at the battery storage sites to provide backup power and enable faster grid restoration.

Today’s announcement comes one year after the United States and Ukraine established URIF’s initial capital base and launched the Fund’s operations, moving URIF from an institutional framework to capital deployment. The Fund made its first investment in emerging-technology company Sine Engineering in March of this year. In June, the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation signed a cooperation agreement with the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) to develop a political risk insurance framework that will catalyze and support private sector investment and capital mobilization in Ukraine in connection with URIF’s investments.

URIF is a joint U.S.–Ukrainian investment fund and a key pillar of the economic partnership between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine. The Fund harnesses American and Ukrainian talent, resources, and expertise to mobilize U.S. and aligned private capital and create strategic investment opportunities in Ukraine for the United States, its allies, multilateral development banks, and private investors. URIF focuses on investments that support Ukraine’s reconstruction, supply chain resilience, and the shared economic security and prosperity of Ukraine and the United States.

For more information and to submit a project proposal, please visit URIF’s website: https://urifinvest.com.

item.title: DFC Highlights U.S. Leadership in Economic Statecraft on Sidelines of U.N. General Assembly
item.description:
DFC Highlights U.S. Leadership in Economic Statecraft on Sidelines of U.N. General Assembly anna.devanny Fri, 09/25/2026 - 14:45
Media Release
September 25, 2026

NEW YORK – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black, Chief of Staff and Head of Investments (HOI) Conor Coleman, and Chief Policy Officer (CPO) Caroline Vik this week attended high-level meetings and engagements on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. DFC engagements highlighted the agency’s unique capabilities to make money for the American taxpayer, meet the strategic interests of the United States, and move the needle for development for our allies and partners.

Ukraine Business Leader Roundtable: 

CEO Black attended a closed-door Ukraine business roundtable with President Zelenskyy, U.S. Government officials, and private sector partners focused on strengthening Ukraine’s economic security.

“President Trump called on DFC, alongside our partners across the U.S. government, to help build the foundation for Ukraine’s economic recovery. The centerpiece of that effort is the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund. I’m grateful to President Zelenskyy, and to the many at DFC, Treasury, and across the Government of Ukraine who work tirelessly against demanding timelines to meet the expectations we set. We are partnering with Ukraine during its most difficult years. We are proud to be a part of this effort and hope for lasting peace”

 

Devex Impact House: 

HOI Coleman participated in a fireside chat with Anna Gawel, managing editor of Devex, at Devex’s Impact House event.

“We’re a big believer that you can do strategic, foreign policy-led investments that make a massive development impact and a financial return all at once. Right now, our pipeline sits at over 300 investments totaling roughly $100 billion. We are in a position to get back to business and get back to doing deals that really make an impact.”

 

U.S.-Argentina Forum: 

CPO Vik attended a State Department and Government of Argentina event for the launch of the Andes-Atlantic Corridor, a joint initiative to strengthen and modernize the infrastructure connecting Argentina’s critical-mineral-rich northwest and Vaca Muerta energy basin to Atlantic ports and Western markets through modern rail, pipeline, port, power, and digital infrastructure. DFC can play a role in financing for high-impact Corridor projects alongside the private sector.

 

Signing Ceremony for DFC’s WIOCC Investment: 

HOI Coleman participated in a signing ceremony for DFC’s recent board approval of an equity investment in WIOCC to strengthen critical digital infrastructure across Africa. The ceremony included Chris Wood, Group CEO of WIOCC, Rayan Alsaedi, Senior Vice President of Digital Infrastructure Investment of Vision, and Sameh Shenouda, Executive Director and Chief Investment Officer, from AFC.

“DFC’s investment in WIOCC Group will help build the next generation of trusted, resilient digital infrastructure needed to power Africa’s economic growth. This platform will not only provide the connectivity that businesses and communities need to participate in the digital economy, but it will also support American and allied partner companies seeking to grow in one of the world’s most dynamic markets, including U.S. hyperscalers and the broader American technology ecosystem.”

 

America First Global Health Strategy Event: 

CPO Vik participated in a panel discussion on co-financing, transition, and the role of the private sector during a high-level dialogue on the State Department's America First Global Health Strategy hosted by the State Department and U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

“Health is a priority sector for DFC. We invest across the value chain in health manufacturing and supply chain, health services and infrastructure, and health technology. Our investments advance U.S. foreign policy priorities to diversify and strengthen regional health supply chains, build resilient health infrastructure, and bolster outbreak response capacity.”

 

Trade Over Aid Deals Showcase: 

CPO Vik participated in a Trade Over Aid Deals Showcase hosted by the United States Mission to the United Nations. During the showcase, she presented three high-impact deals DFC has advanced over the last year that have promoted mutually beneficial foreign trade and long-term economic resilience.

“Our partners need infrastructure, energy, technology, and capital to grow – and we can provide it, while generating returns for the American taxpayer. DFC’s recently approved investments in WIOCC, an equity investment to strengthen critical digital infrastructure across Africa, in Cambodia’s new Techo International Airport, one of the country’s most important strategic infrastructure assets, and in our new U.S. Trade Finance Support Facility with the IFC, which will help facilitate the purchase of American goods abroad, are perfect examples of Trade Over Aid in practice.”

 

These remarks have been lightly edited for clarity.

item.title: DFC CEO Ben Black Discusses Global Energy and Telecom Investments at Semafor’s Next 3 Billion Summit
item.description:
DFC CEO Ben Black Discusses Global Energy and Telecom Investments at Semafor’s Next 3 Billion Summit anna.devanny Tue, 09/22/2026 - 18:09
Media Release
September 22, 2026

NEW YORK – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black today highlighted DFC’s efforts to build up energy infrastructure and telecom networks during Semafor’s Next 3 Billion Summit in New York City. The conversation was moderated by Prashant Rao, global managing editor at Semafor.

 

On developing energy infrastructure: 

“The U.S. is the largest producer of crude and natural gas in the world, and a massive exporter of it... So what does it mean to help export U.S. gas and make sure that our allies and friends have energy security? It really goes down the chain and you have to look at some types of vertical integration to make sure you’re covering the ports, you’re covering the terminals, you’re covering the pipelines and power generation, and that fits so well with American business. If you look at the I Squared deal we did at our previous board, that’s going to unlock $17 billion worth of U.S. exports in LNG.”

On DFC’s WIOCC deal to create safe and secure telecoms networks in Africa: 

“Our WIOCC deal is a a pan-African equity investment, and actually at the time, the largest equity deal DFC had done. What it allows for is the continued building of networks, cloud infrastructure, and a lot of telecoms ability to run on U.S. pipes. And as we get to AI investment and the future of technology across Africa, not building on U.S. friendly rails would be madness.”

On DFC’s investment thesis: 

“We are looking to make money for the American taxpayer, meet the strategic interests of the United States, and move the needle for development for our allies and partners... Our guiding light, my metric is: is this good for the American people? Are we serving the interests of the U.S. people broadly? I think that does stand the test of time. Because ultimately the U.S. is here as the greatest friend to other nations, freedom for investment and to open markets, and I think it benefits American citizens at the same time.”

These remarks have been lightly edited for clarity.

item.title: DFC Announces More Than $8 Billion in Investments to Fuel American Economic and National Security Interests
item.description:
DFC Announces More Than $8 Billion in Investments to Fuel American Economic and National Security Interests danielle.hawkins Tue, 09/15/2026 - 10:43
Media Release
September 16, 2026

Washington, D.C. – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) Board of Directors today approved more than $8 billion in new investments, representing a significant milestone for the agency. The investments advance President Trump’s commitment to strengthen and increase trade between the United States and its allies. Since reauthorization, DFC has utilized strategic capital to reinforce U.S. economic and national security interests. These new projects will secure essential services in partner nations while prioritizing American export growth, securing reliable energy, and advancing U.S. technology, including DFC’s largest digital investment to date.

“These are exactly the kinds of investments President Trump empowered DFC to make. These projects will support billions in American exports, secure critical infrastructure and resources in Ukraine, Jordan, and across Africa, and strengthen U.S. companies competing in some of the most important markets in the world,” said Ben Black, DFC CEO.

The DFC Board of Directors approved the following deals:

  • Increasing U.S. Exports to Emerging Markets: DFC will support U.S. exports by providing a counter-guaranty to the International Finance Corporation (IFC) for its Global Trade Finance Program, which will empower foreign banks to expand their trade finance capabilities and facilitate the purchase of American goods within their respective countries. Through this innovative partnership, DFC will share risk with the IFC on trade finance guaranties issued exclusively for U.S. exports, helping American companies to realize billions of dollars in international transactions to new markets. The project will also enhance the trade finance offerings of local banks and increase the developmental benefits for their countries that come from greater trade.
  • Bringing Trusted Technology to Ukraine’s Digital Infrastructure: DFC will provide financing to Vodafone Ukraine, the country’s second-largest mobile operator, and a wholly owned subsidiary of the NEQSOL Holding, to strengthen and modernize critical telecommunications infrastructure during the ongoing war. U.S. companies operating and investing in Ukraine will also benefit from access to secure and reliable network infrastructure built increasingly around trusted technology.
  • Strengthening Ukraine’s Energy Security with American Technology: DFC’s financing will support a 200MW/400MWh battery energy storage systems portfolio across six sites in Ukraine, providing the power grid with greater resilience and stability. This project, developed by DTEK in partnership with technology from U.S.-based company Fluence, will provide critical services to regulate frequency, balance fluctuations, and increase energy security. The system will provide enough power for 600,000 homes for two hours.
  • Bolstering U.S. and Jordanian Security Through Water Infrastructure: DFC is proud to support a transformational investment in Jordan’s critical infrastructure. Today, DFC’s Board of Directors approved a loan to the National Carrier Project Company and political risk insurance for the equity investors, Meridiam and Suez. The loan will advance the construction, operation, and maintenance of a seawater desalination plant and conveyance system in Jordan, the world’s second-most water-scarce country. Enabling Jordan’s long-term water security by expanding access to new water resources will support economic growth, expand regional connectivity, and enhance stability for a key U.S. ally.
  • Expanding U.S. Technology Across Sub-Saharan Africa: DFC will provide an equity investment to WIOCC Group to strengthen critical digital infrastructure across Africa. This investment aligns with U.S. strategic interests in supporting U.S. hyperscalers and the American technology ecosystem, while extending availability of secure, affordable, and resilient digital infrastructure across the African continent. WIOCC Group is the preferred partner for U.S. technology companies expanding in Africa, operating an open-access and carrier-neutral platform that provides wholesale connectivity, data center, and metro-fiber services. The platform’s footprint spans 30 African countries, including subsea cables, terrestrial fiber networks, and more than 40 core and edge data centers. DFC’s investment partners for this initiative include Vision International Investment Company and the Africa Finance Corporation.

DFC is also supporting a critical minerals project in West Africa. Additional transactions remain confidential due to commercial sensitivities and may be subject to further steps before commitment and closing, including congressional notification.

Please find more information on the DFC Board of Directors web page.

item.title: DFC Announces Approval of Financing for Project to Support U.S.-Honduras Commercial Engagement
item.description:
DFC Announces Approval of Financing for Project to Support U.S.-Honduras Commercial Engagement anna.devanny Wed, 09/09/2026 - 09:03
Media Release
September 9, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) yesterday announced project approval for a $10 million loan to Financiera MiCrédito Honduras, S.A., a majority U.S.-owned financial institution in Honduras, to support on-lending to eligible micro, small, and medium-sized businesses. At least 50% of loan proceeds will support U.S.-Honduran trade by financing the procurement of eligible U.S. goods and services and strengthening U.S. supply chains.

Project approval was recognized with a signing ceremony in Washington, D.C. between DFC Chief Policy Officer (CPO) Caroline Vik and MiCrédito Holding Corp Regional CEO Verónica Herrera, witnessed by Honduran Finance Minister Emilio Hernández Hércules, Central Bank President Roberto Lagos, and Trade Representative Melvin Redondo.

“I am excited to see DFC approve this investment in Financiera MiCrédito Honduras. Building on our recent engagement in Tegucigalpa, this project reflects the strength of the U.S.-Honduras partnership – supporting entrepreneurs while deepening trade ties, strengthening supply chain linkages, and creating new opportunities for Honduran businesses to connect with U.S. goods and markets,” said DFC CPO Caroline Vik.

“This partnership with DFC is an important vote of confidence in Honduras and its entrepreneurs. We are grateful to DFC and the Government of Honduras for advancing investment and economic growth. Through this partnership, MiCrédito will expand responsible financing for Honduran businesses, helping them grow, create jobs, and strengthen their families and communities,” said Verónica Herrera, MiCrédito Holding Corp Regional CEO.

Earlier this year, DFC CEO Ben Black and CPO Vik visited Tegucigalpa to meet with President Nasry Asfura and cabinet officials to discuss opportunities for U.S.-Honduras engagement. This facility deepens commercial ties by expanding access to financing for thousands of micro, small, and medium-sized businesses in Honduras purchasing U.S. agricultural inputs and manufactured goods, including tractors and harvest equipment, irrigation and pumping systems, and fertilizers distributed by U.S. companies.

item.title: DFC Announces Financing for Madagascar Rare Earths Project
item.description:
DFC Announces Financing for Madagascar Rare Earths Project danielle.hawkins Fri, 08/07/2026 - 09:47
Media Release
August 7, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) today announced it will provide project development funding for the Harena Rare Earths plc (LSE: HREE, OTCQB: CRMNF) rare earth mine in Madagascar. The funding, announced during the American Mining Industry event held at U.S. Department State, marks DFC’s first mining investment in Madagascar, advances the development of a strategically important source of rare earth elements essential to U.S. advanced manufacturing, and builds on DFC’s strategic portfolio of rare earths assets, including Serra Verra and Aclara, that aim to secure U.S. and allied partners’ supply chains.

“President Trump is looking out for the American people and has made securing our critical mineral supply chains a national priority. Through projects like Harena, DFC is helping expand America’s access to these essential materials and providing our partners transparent, high-quality financing alternatives. DFC is proud to support investments that strengthen U.S. economic security and create lasting economic opportunity for both the United States and Madagascar,” said Ben Black, DFC CEO.

“This investment by the U.S. government through the DFC is a huge endorsement of the quality of our ionic clay rare earth project in Madagascar. We are deeply grateful to Ben Black and Conor Coleman for their leadership of DFC, as well as to the teams with whom we have had the pleasure of working with. We are honored to be playing our part to alleviate the chronic shortage of magnet metal and heavy rare earths and to increase mineral security for the United States and its partners,” said Ivan Murphy, Harena Resources Executive Chairman.

Rare earth elements are critical to the technologies that support advanced manufacturing and U.S. national security, including high-performance permanent magnets and precision-guided defense systems. DFC’s project development funding helps turn promising ventures into investment-ready projects that are profitable for the American taxpayer and U.S. businesses and help diversify and secure critical U.S. supply chains.

DFC’s strategy in Africa prioritizes investments in vital sectors, including mining, that enable African nations to unlock their vast economic potential while strengthening America’s strategic partnerships, supply chain resilience, and long-term economic competitiveness.

###  

About the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation

The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.

About Harena Resources

Harena is a rare earths development company focused on the Ampasindava Ionic Clay Rare Earth Project in Madagascar (Harena's interest is 100%). The project hosts one of the largest ionic clay rare earth deposits outside of China, with significant concentrations of high-value magnet metals, specifically heavy rare earths, including neodymium (Nd), dysprosium (Dy), and praseodymium (Pr), which are critical for the composition of neodymium magnets (NdFeB). Harena is committed to low-impact, high recovery mining, providing a sustainable supply of critical minerals for technology and military defence industries as well as meeting the ever-growing demand for NdFeB from the robotics sector. 

Learn more at: https://harenaresources.com/

item.title: DFC CEO Ben Black Gives Opening Remarks at Hearing on Ending Supply Chain Dependency
item.description:
DFC CEO Ben Black Gives Opening Remarks at Hearing on Ending Supply Chain Dependency anna.devanny Tue, 07/14/2026 - 14:43
Media Release
July 15, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black today gave the following opening remarks at a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing entitled “Ending Supply Chain Dependency: Aligning Tools, Capital, and Partnership.”

Remarks as delivered:

“Thank you, Chairman Mast, Ranking Member Meeks, and members of the committee for this opportunity to discuss DFC’s efforts to end supply chain dependency. I’m proud to be here today to represent the hundreds of committed professionals at DFC who work every day to advance our mission.

“I would also like to thank you all for your bipartisan support of DFC’s December reauthorization. Under President Trump’s leadership, DFC is equipped to be a leading force for restoring U.S. economic security. We now have $205 billion of investment capacity and a greater ability to deploy debt, equity, and insurance across the capital stack. DFC can invest in technology, energy, and critical minerals nearly anywhere in the world, and address vulnerable supply chains wherever they exist.

“Since reauthorization, DFC has rebuilt our pipeline to more than 340 deal opportunities totaling $78 billion across agriculture, healthcare, financial services, energy, technology, and critical minerals. We are focused on regions vital to U.S. economic security like the Western Hemisphere, East Asia and the Pacific, Central Asia, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, amongst others.

“As CEO of DFC, I have made it my mission to transform DFC into a best-in-class financial institution. We have begun a rigorous process to value our entire portfolio dating back to the OPIC days, and intend to dynamically share investment performance for all administrations – both previous and future. I’m also pleased to report we have reduced investment timelines by an average of 10 weeks.

“More importantly, I have sought to align DFC’s investment strategy with the enduring principles of American economic statecraft. American economic statecraft – the use of our nation’s economic and financial power to guarantee our strategic interests – has guided America through its greatest moments. Alexander Hamilton understood that strong financial institutions and the ability to produce essential goods are vital to securing America’s global position. That tradition gave rise to the Panama Canal, and later inspired the Marshall Plan, which rebuilt war-torn Europe, anchored European markets to the American system, and delivered decades of stability and growth.

“Today, I want to highlight how DFC is building on that tradition of success.

“First, DFC will directly challenge our adversaries in the most strategically contested sectors by financing transactions that diplomacy and private markets alone cannot deliver.

“Last month, we announced a monumental agreement for one of Kazakhstan’s largest telecom networks to expand access to U.S.-aligned, trusted service providers. We are committed to helping others adopt this model, especially in the Western Hemisphere, where China’s Digital Silk Road cannot entrench its influence.

“Second, DFC will prioritize large, capital-intensive projects. Our goal is to build holistic economic ecosystems anchored to U.S. capital markets and structured to create returns for American taxpayers and meaningful economic development for our allies.

“DFC’s $553 million loan to restore the Lobito Atlantic Railway exemplifies the $1.5 billion DFC has committed across Africa since my confirmation. This vital transportation corridor connects the mineral-rich Democratic Republic of Congo, through Zambia, to the port of Lobito in Angola. DFC financing will help establish a western-aligned source of critical minerals and also strengthen local trade by reducing the costs of shipping by as much as 30 percent.

“Throughout human civilization, industrialization has been the single greatest force for lifting people out of poverty. Industrialization depends on reliable energy, a sector that is vital to America’s interests as the world’s leading producer and exporter of oil and natural gas. In June, DFC’s Board approved $1.5 billion for energy infrastructure across South and Southeast Asia, ensuring U.S. LNG and American equipment help power the energy needs of a strategic region.

“Finally, we are mobilizing private capital through sophisticated financial structures that reduce risk for investors and create enduring American influence in critical sectors and regions.

“That approach underpins our $600 million contribution to the $1.8 billion Critical Minerals Consortium with Orion Resource Partners. DFC’s Board recently approved an additional $900 million of financing to support Orion CMC’s rapidly expanding pipeline of mining and minerals opportunities to help address China’s strategic chokehold.

“DFC’s U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund, or URIF, is another example. This $150 million joint fund is mobilizing private investment in Ukraine’s recovery and can provide a blueprint for DFC investment in other regions vital to America’s long-term interests.

“Our partners want to work with us because our model is better. America’s most transformative economic partnerships were built through the power of private investment, the discipline of capital markets, and the laser focus of finance. The Trump Administration’s restoration of American economic statecraft will guarantee our country’s success.

“Thank you, and I look forward to your questions.”

item.title: CEO Ben Black Shares Insights on “Exporting the AI Stack” at Pax Silica Summit
item.description:
CEO Ben Black Shares Insights on “Exporting the AI Stack” at Pax Silica Summit danielle.hawkins Fri, 06/26/2026 - 11:48
Media Release
June 25, 2026

 

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) CEO Ben Black participated in the “Exporting the AI Stack” panel discussion at the two-day Pax Silica Summit hosted by Under Secretary of Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg at the U.S. Department of State. CEO Black was joined by International Trade Administration Deputy Under Secretary Bill Guidera, Chair of the President’s Council of Advisors in Science and Technology David Sacks, U.S. Senator Jim Risch, and other top AI industry leaders. This panel brought together two initiatives, Pax Silica and the Commerce-led American AI Exports Program to address key challenges and expand the burden-sharing needed for success, including private capital and grant funding from Pax Silica member countries.

“President Trump has challenged us to make sure America is the partner of choice for countries looking to compete in the global race for AI. It is encouraging to see so many of our AI industry leaders and global partners here ready to answer that call.

“Since my confirmation as CEO of DFC last October, the number one request I have received from our partners has been for investment in AI data centers. The opportunities being created by AI are significant but realizing them requires substantial investment in its supporting infrastructure.

“The choices countries make today about telecom networks, fiber systems, data centers, cloud infrastructure, and power generation will not only shape their economic competitiveness, but ours as well. For example, secure telecommunications networks are an essential prerequisite for attracting global investors and best-in-class businesses.

“That is why supporting trusted vendors who can support next generation technology and AI is so important to DFC. Our allies want to partner with the best American technologies and AI industry leaders, but the American AI stack cannot be built on a compromised foundation.

“China understands the stakes. Through its Digital Silk Road, China uses aggressive financing and subsidized offerings to entrench its influence across digital systems worldwide. Their model creates long term dependencies that limit choice, undermine resilience, and target the United States.

“The focus of today’s gathering is to offer a better alternative. That is why the DFC exists. DFC was created by President Trump in his first term as a powerful tool to counter China’s Belt and Road Initiative. As the international investment arm of the United States Government, our mission is to mobilize private capital to advance U.S. strategic interests and strengthen our allies and partners. Our goal is to build holistic economic ecosystems anchored to U.S. capital markets, insulated against adversary control, and structured to generate strong returns for the American taxpayer.

“Following our reauthorization last year, DFC now has 205 billion dollars of investment capacity and a greater ability to deploy debt, equity, and insurance across the capital stack and investment structures. Importantly, we can now invest in technology and energy anywhere in the world, and we can address vulnerable supply chains wherever they exist.

“We know U.S. led efforts in Costa Rica and Paraguay have kept Huawei out of new 5G networks. I want to congratulate my interagency colleagues for this important accomplishment, and I agree that malign influences must stay out of the Western Hemisphere.

“And this extends around the world. I recently returned from Kazakhstan, one of the newest Pax Silica partners, where DFC announced a partnership alongside PIH, the parent company of one of the country’s largest telecommunications providers.

“This monumental deal will expand access to trusted, U.S.-aligned service providers – and I would like to thank Ericsson for everything they’ve done to support this effort. We know that it is not always easy or costless for our partners to prioritize long-term supply chain resilience and security. We know they face tremendous pressure and retaliation when attempting to diversify their equipment providers and concentrated telecom networks.

“DFC is determined to help our partners make those choices with confidence. U.S. government financing is ready to help meet the growing global demand for the trusted American AI technology stack, from data centers focused on both training and inference, to terrestrial fiber and subsea cables required to move data at scale. While the backbone for the AI era is trusted networks, we can secure the energy supply as well.

“DFC’s financial products are uniquely suited to support capital-intensive projects required for AI’s growth, including power generation, transmission infrastructure, and grid modernization. Our insurance products alone can mobilize private investment in sums that dwarf our own balance sheet – and that of our adversaries.

“The U.S. government is united behind this mission. America has the most advanced – and the best – technology the world has to offer. We are home to the most innovative entrepreneurs and companies. If we work together with our trusted vendors and strong allies, I am confident that we can meet the challenge ahead.”

###  

The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.

item.title: DFC, MIGA Sign Agreement to Advance Political Risk Insurance in Ukraine
item.description:
DFC, MIGA Sign Agreement to Advance Political Risk Insurance in Ukraine anna.devanny Wed, 06/24/2026 - 17:43
Media Release
June 25, 2026

GDAŃSK, Poland – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) today signed a cooperation agreement with the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), the home of the World Bank Group Guarantee Platform, to establish a political risk insurance (PRI) framework for the United States-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund (URIF). This framework is intended to catalyze and support opportunities for private sector investment and mobilization in Ukraine in connection with the fund’s investments.

“Today’s agreement with MIGA marks another important milestone with URIF and furthers the goal of accelerating Ukraine’s recovery and long-term economic resilience,” said Conor Coleman, DFC Chief of Staff and Head of Investments. “Now the fund is not only making active investments, but fulfilling its original commitment to mobilize additional co-investment vehicles alongside the platform. By aligning DFC’s and MIGA’s expertise, tools, and risk-mitigation capabilities, we can deliver more coordinated PRI solutions that give investors the confidence to pursue high-impact opportunities in Ukraine through URIF.”

“Guarantees will be critical in mobilizing the private investment Ukraine needs to finance its recovery and reconstruction,” said Ed Mountfield, MIGA Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. “We are proud to increase our support to Ukraine through this partnership with DFC, which will help to strengthen the country’s business environment, mobilize private capital, and increase economic resilience, while creating and protecting jobs.”

The cooperation convention was signed on the sidelines of the Ukraine Reconstruction Conference in Gdańsk, Poland by Coleman and Mountfield. The signing was witnessed by Ajay Banga, President of the World Bank Group; Oleksii Sobolev, Minister of Economy for Ukraine; and Jonathan Greenstein, Under Secretary for International Affairs at the U.S. Treasury Department.

Background on DFC’s PRI

Since 1974, DFC has issued more than 3,000 PRI policies in 152 countries totaling over $59 billion. DFC’s PRI provides coverage against losses due to currency inconvertibility, expropriation and takings, and political violence, including terrorism.

###  

About DFC: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) is the international investment arm of the United States Government and central to U.S. economic statecraft. DFC mobilizes private capital to advance U.S. foreign policy and economic development. Our investments deliver strong returns for American taxpayers, drive meaningful economic development for our allies and partners, and secure supply chains to counter and outcompete our adversaries.    

About the World Bank Group Guarantee Platform: Initiated in 2024, the World Bank Group Guarantee Platform consolidates guarantee products and experts from across the World Bank Group at MIGA. It provides a simplified and comprehensive menu of guarantee solutions, enabling clients to select the instrument that best suits their needs. The platform streamlines processes, removes redundancies, and provides greater accessibility by de-risking investments in developing countries.    

About URIF: URIF is a key pillar of the Trump administration’s economic partnership with Ukraine, harnessing American talent, resources, and governance to mobilize U.S. and aligned capital and create strategic investment opportunities for the United States, its allies, multilateral development banks, and other investors. The Fund is focusing on investments that support supply chain resilience and shared U.S. and Ukrainian economic security and prosperity.
